# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

package net.officefloor.hq.app.person;

import java.util.List;

/** statementCount is how many statements were taken; statedTotal is the last one's due-total ("n/a" when it
 *  was n/a, "" when none was taken); statementDate is the sheet's today when it was taken ("" when none); retired says whether a retirement date is set and retiredFrom is it ("" when none); held says whether they have any hold and holds lists each (from, to; to "" when open-ended), in the order added; patrons are the names of the people they named as patrons, sorted, and patronIds their ids; grade is the grade in force on the sheet's today and grades every grade recorded, by from-date; terms is the person's own terms in days ("" for none); contact is the person's contact ("" for none); tags are the person's tags, sorted and comma separated ("" for none); aliases are the person's aliases, sorted as names are compared; clashing says whether their name or an alias is used by someone else on a sheet of the sheet's tree; origin is the sheet they were transferred from ("" for none); retirements are their past retirements, each "<from> to <to>", in the order they ended; snapshots are their SNAPSHOT lines, each "<the day being left> <due-total>", oldest first. */
public record PersonResponse(String id, String name, String grade, int version, int statementCount,
        String statedTotal, String statementDate, boolean retired, String retiredFrom, boolean held,
        List<HoldFrom> holds,
        List<String> patrons, List<String> patronIds, List<GradeFrom> grades, String terms, String contact, String tags,
        List<String> aliases, boolean clashing, String origin, List<String> retirements, List<String> snapshots) {

    /** A grade in force from a date (YYYY-MM-DD; "" for the beginning of time). */
    public record GradeFrom(String from, String grade) {
    }

    /** A hold from a date to a date (YYYY-MM-DD; to "" when open-ended). */
    public record HoldFrom(String from, String to) {
    }

    public static PersonResponse from(Person person) {
        boolean stated = person.getStatementCount() > 0;
        return new PersonResponse(String.valueOf(person.getId()), person.getName(), person.getGrade(), person.getVersion(),
                person.getStatementCount(),
                !stated ? "" : person.getStatedTotal() == null ? "n/a" : person.getStatedTotal().setScale(2).toPlainString(),
                person.getStatementDate() == null ? "" : person.getStatementDate().toString(),
                person.isRetired(), person.getRetiredFrom() == null ? "" : person.getRetiredFrom().toString(),
                person.isHeld(),
                person.getHolds().stream().map(h -> new HoldFrom(h.from().toString(), h.to() == null ? "" : h.to().toString())).toList(),
                List.copyOf(person.getPatronNames()),
                person.getPatronIds().stream().map(String::valueOf).toList(),
                person.getGrades().entrySet().stream().map(e -> new GradeFrom(
                        e.getKey().equals(Person.BEGINNING) ? "" : e.getKey().toString(), e.getValue())).toList(),
                person.getTerms() == null ? "" : String.valueOf(person.getTerms()),
                person.getContact() == null ? "" : person.getContact(),
                person.getTags() == null ? "" : person.getTags(),
                List.copyOf(person.getAliases()), person.isClashing(),
                person.getOrigin() == null ? "" : person.getOrigin(),
                person.getRetirements().stream().map(r -> r.from() + " to " + r.to()).toList(),
                List.copyOf(person.getSnapshots()));
    }

    public static List<PersonResponse> from(List<Person> people) {
        return people.stream().map(PersonResponse::from).toList();
    }
}

 *  was n/a, "" when none was taken); statementDate is the sheet's today when it was taken ("" when none); retired says whether a retirement date is set and retiredFrom is it ("" when none); held says whether they have any hold and holds lists each (from, to; to "" when open-ended), in the order added; patrons are the names of the people they named as patrons, sorted, and patronIds their ids; grade is the grade in force on the sheet's today and grades every grade recorded, by from-date; terms is the person's own terms in days ("" for none); contact is the person's contact ("" for none); tags are the person's tags, sorted and comma separated ("" for none); aliases are the person's aliases, sorted as names are compared; clashing says whether their name or an alias is used by someone else on a sheet of the sheet's tree; origin is the sheet they were transferred from ("" for none); retirements are their past retirements, each "<from> to <to>", in the order they ended; snapshots are their SNAPSHOT lines, each "<the day being left> <due-total>", oldest first. */
public record PersonResponse(String id, String name, String grade, int version, int statementCount,
        String statedTotal, String statementDate, boolean retired, String retiredFrom, boolean held,
        List<HoldFrom> holds,
        List<String> patrons, List<String> patronIds, List<GradeFrom> grades, String terms, String contact, String tags,
        List<String> aliases, boolean clashing, String origin, List<String> retirements, List<String> snapshots) {

    /** A grade in force from a date (YYYY-MM-DD; "" for the beginning of time). */
    public record GradeFrom(String from, String grade) {
    }

    /** A hold from a date to a date (YYYY-MM-DD; to "" when open-ended). */
    public record HoldFrom(String from, String to) {
    }

    public static PersonResponse from(Person person) {
        boolean stated = person.getStatementCount() > 0;
        return new PersonResponse(String.valueOf(person.getId()), person.getName(), person.getGrade(), person.getVersion(),
                person.getStatementCount(),
                !stated ? "" : person.getStatedTotal() == null ? "n/a" : person.getStatedTotal().setScale(2).toPlainString(),
                person.getStatementDate() == null ? "" : person.getStatementDate().toString(),
                person.isRetired(), person.getRetiredFrom() == null ? "" : person.getRetiredFrom().toString(),
                person.isHeld(),
                person.getHolds().stream().map(h -> new HoldFrom(h.from().toString(), h.to() == null ? "" : h.to().toString())).toList(),
                List.copyOf(person.getPatronNames()),
                person.getPatronIds().stream().map(String::valueOf).toList(),
                person.getGrades().entrySet().stream().map(e -> new GradeFrom(
                        e.getKey().equals(Person.BEGINNING) ? "" : e.getKey().toString(), e.getValue())).toList(),
                person.getTerms() == null ? "" : String.valueOf(person.getTerms()),
                person.getContact() == null ? "" : person.getContact(),
                person.getTags() == null ? "" : person.getTags(),
                List.copyOf(person.getAliases()), person.isClashing(),
                person.getOrigin() == null ? "" : person.getOrigin(),
                person.getRetirements().stream().map(r -> r.from() + " to " + r.to()).toList(),
                List.copyOf(person.getSnapshots()));
    }

    public static List<PersonResponse> from(List<Person> people) {
        return people.stream().map(PersonResponse::from).toList();
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL. A loaded
# machine can take minutes to bring the JVM up; running the specs before it is ready fails every
# one of them for no reason, so wait long and fail loudly rather than run against nothing.
ready=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done

I've added the statement lines to each person, but `bin/e2e` does not fully pass: 3 of the 4 tests pass, and "statement lines scenario 2" still fails. The failure is in an as-of-date claim figure that my change doesn't touch.

**What I changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V86__statement_brought.sql`, adds a `brought` flag to the statement history table. Before, a merge or transfer copied the other person's statements only if the receiving person had none of their own. Now they are always copied, and flagged `brought` when the receiving person already had some.
- **Server:** each person now carries a list of their statements, one line per statement as `<statement date> <due-total>` (`n/a` when there was no figure). Cancelled ones are left out, and the list is sorted oldest first by date, so brought-over statements fall among the person's own. This works in both the normal view and the as-of-date view (`People.java`, `AsOfView.java`, `Person.java`, `PersonResponse.java`).
- **Existing behaviour kept:** a brought-over statement is never counted as the person's "last" statement, so the last stated total and date, and which statement a cancel removes first, work as before. Once only brought-over statements are left, a cancel removes the newest of those, so the count and the lines stay in step.
- **Front end:** a new column in the people list shows each line in a `person-statement-line-line` element (`PeopleList.tsx`, `usePeople.ts`).

**The scenario 2 failure**
Line 800 expects a claim's due as of 2026-03-20 to be `1.29` but gets `n/a`. The rate that gives 1.29 is set on the parent sheet, and the test never sets that sheet's date. A new sheet starts on the real date (2026-10-31), so the rate is recorded as set on that day. The as-of view only uses rates set by the end of the chosen day, so it correctly leaves this one out. The expected value only works if the test runs on or before 2026-03-20.

As a check, I temporarily made that rate lookup ignore the as-of date. The test then got past line 800 and failed at line 877: the as-of view shows a blank "reminded" date where `2026-03-20` is expected, which is also unrelated to statements. I put the rate lookup back as it was. Every statement-line check before line 877 passed. The last two (lines 1069 and 1131) come after that point and have not been run.

I left both of these alone because fixing them would change how the as-of view works, which is outside this request. Say if you want me to take them on.
